title: Path reuse before physical module birth
hypothesis: On sequential tasks with a recurring rotated function plus occasional off-orbit functions, a support-selected Givens View of a frozen PathNet module can avoid physical module births while preserving per-task query quality and retention better than path-only reuse.
physical_object: frozen 2x2 linear modules learned from task support
mirror_coordinate: one per-task output Givens angle applied to a selected module
logical_multiplicity: task-specific linear maps from reused physical module paths and Views
controls: PathNet-style path-only module reuse with birth on failed validation
Mirror-view reuse then private module birth on failed validation

task.distribution: task0 is canonical A0; tasks1-23 are output rotations of A0; tasks24-31 are rotated off-orbit perturbations with changed singular values
task.adaptation: least-squares module fit on support; route against frozen modules; birth a private matrix if validation NRMSE exceeds threshold
task.retention: re-evaluate all prior task paths after the sequence, with frozen modules

development.selection: choose highest threshold with <=0.03 mean query NRMSE for both path-only and Mirror on dev

success_gate: Every fresh world: Mirror retains >=95% query quality of always-private (NRMSE <=1.05x), has no worse prior-task retention, and births <=50% as many modules as PathNet while using <=75% of PathNet actual payload bytes at N=32.
failure_gate: Mirror fails quality/retention, module births exceed half the PathNet count, N32 payload exceeds 75% of PathNet, or improvement is matched by path-only routing.
boundaries: Aligned synthetic rotation reuse plus controlled off-orbit module birth; not natural continual learning.
Task sequence and boundaries are provided, but module/path identity is not.
All support, route, and private matrix state is serialized and charged.
